results.title: UN chief calls for action to deal with extreme heat
results.description: United Nations, Aug 1 (IANS) UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres called for action to deal with extreme heat caused by El Nino. The UN chief made the appeal at a press encounter on Friday, citing an update on El Nino forecasts released by the World Meteorological Organization (WMO). According to the new forecasts, this summer's extremes -- record-shattering heat domes, apocalyptic wildfires, thousands of lives lost in scorching conditions, record-high global sea-surface temperatures -- are only a warm-up act, said Guterres. El Nino is strengthening, adding fuel to a planet already on fire. The Pacific waters driving the phenomenon have never been this warm this early in an El Nino and temperatures are still rising, he said. "At the same time, WMO's outlook shows that through October, nearly every land area on Earth is expected to be hotter than normal." El Nino does not bring heat alone; it profoundly affects the world's rainfall. India's monsoon is already running well below average. Hotter and drier conditions are forecast from Central America and the Caribbean to parts of South America, South Asia, the Southwest Pacific, Europe and Africa, warned Guterres, Xinhua news agency reported. "The verdict is clear: the climate crisis is in overdrive," he said. The UN chief called for action on four fronts: protect people before heat becomes deadlier, make work safer, build and retrofit for the coming heat, and stop fueling the climate crisis. Extreme heat is a society-wide threat that demands a government-wide response. Every city and country should have heat-health action plans, early warning systems and public health measures that reach every community in time. And access to sustainable cooling must expand urgently and equitably, he said. Governments and employers must set heat standards, adjust working hours, and protect incomes when work must stop. Protection from extreme heat must be designed into cities, homes, schools and hospitals, and factored into every plan and public budget, he said. Guterres warned that every new fossil fuel project approved today makes tomorrow's heatwaves more dangerous, and the world less secure. "Today's findings show that extreme heat is not a future threat. It is here. It is becoming more dangerous. And unless we act -- to protect people and tackle the root cause of the crisis -- it will become deadlier still," he said. "The warm-up act is over. We cannot afford to wait for the main event." --IANS int/rs

results.title: LoP Sunil Sharma meets LG, seeks justice for left-out sportspersons
results.description: Leader of Opposition in the Jammu & Kashmir Legislative Assembly, Sunil Sharma, along with Billawar MLA Satish Sharma, on Friday met Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha and discussed a range of issues related to sports, religious affairs, infrastructure development and public welfare in the Union Territory. During the meeting, the BJP leaders raised concerns over the reported exclusion of several accomplished sportspersons from Jammu and Kashmir from the recently announced selection list. They specifically highlighted the cases of deserving para-athletes and Arjuna Award recipients, stating that these athletes have brought laurels to both Jammu and Kashmir and the country through their achievements. The delegation urged the Lieutenant Governor to ensure that all deserving sportspersons are duly recognised and provided the benefits, support and opportunities they rightfully deserve. The leaders also took up issues concerning the Shri Sukrala Mata Shrine Board, stressing the need to strengthen the Board and undertake measures to improve infrastructure and pilgrim amenities. They said better facilities and planned development would help establish the shrine as a major religious and tourism destination in the region. In addition, Sharma and Satish Sharma apprised the Lieutenant Governor of several issues concerning infrastructure development, public welfare, tourism, road connectivity and the timely execution of ongoing developmental projects across different parts of Jammu and Kashmir. They sought expeditious intervention to ensure that development projects are completed without delay and that the benefits of development reach all regions of the Union Territory in a balanced and inclusive manner. The delegation emphasised that improved infrastructure, enhanced connectivity and accelerated implementation of public projects are essential for promoting economic growth, boosting tourism and improving the quality of life of the people. Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha gave a patient hearing to the issues raised by the delegation and assured them that all genuine concerns would be examined on priority. He also assured the leaders that appropriate directions would be issued to the concerned departments to facilitate timely action. Following the meeting, Sunil Sharma thanked the Lieutenant Governor for his positive response and expressed confidence that the issues highlighted by the delegation, particularly those concerning deserving sportspersons, the development of the Shri Sukrala Mata Shrine Board and the acceleration of developmental works, would receive due consideration in the larger interest of the people of Jammu and Kashmir.

results.title: Six months after Nancy Guthrie's disappearance, no arrests made and ransom notes released
results.description: Six months since Nancy Guthrie was last seen in Tucson, Pima County Sheriff Chris Nanos sat down for a one-on-one interview with ABC15’s Ford Hatchett this week, reiterating that the case is not cold. Guthrie, 84, mother of NBC "Today" anchor Savannah Guthrie, was last seen at her home on the evening of Jan. 31. Her disappearance has drawn national attention and sparked a months-long investigation involving the Pima County Sheriff's Department, the FBI and private forensic labs across the country. Nanos said investigators are still analyzing DNA recovered from the home, though he declined to say where at the residence it was found, citing the integrity of the investigation.
